core.title: Cached or incremental results: define reuse-safety contracts
core.given: Work includes an expensive, repeatable read or derivation with stable identities and tractable dependencies
core.when: deciding to reuse its results or recompute only affected portions
core.then: Reuse valid results, or recompute only affected portions, only where you define cache key, freshness, invalidation, authorization, tenant isolation and side-effect contracts that make reuse safe; a hit must never omit a required permission check or mutation.
prefer: Reuse only where freshness and invalidation contracts make it safe.
avoid: A cache hit that skips a required permission check or mutation.
core.why: Unsafe reuse serves stale, cross-tenant or unauthorized results and silently skips required mutations.
evidence: The plan states cache key, freshness, invalidation, authorization, tenant isolation and side-effect handling for the reused or incrementally recomputed result.
Every planned hit path still performs required permission checks and mutations.
verification: Advisory guidance: severity 3, disposition advisory — not independent enforcement; the stack's existing plan and source checks still apply.
Check that no planned hit path omits a required permission or mutation.

values: expensive repeatable read or derivation with stable identity and tractable dependencies
facts.note: REQUIRED. All four criteria (expensive, repeatable, stable identity, tractable dependencies) must hold; judged from the work content whether or not caching is mentioned. No phase restriction.
OPTIONAL hint only: raises priority; neither necessary nor sufficient.

fires: A component repeatedly performs an expensive read keyed by a stable identity with tractable dependencies.
An expensive derived result is requested repeatedly and only parts change between requests (incremental recompute candidate).
doesNotFire: A cheap read where recomputation costs nothing meaningful.
Reads without stable identity or with intractable dependencies (outside this pattern's applicability; no guidance given for them).

bunOnly.reason: Pointer to a shared policy entry id of this rule corpus that encodes the advisory semantics; ids of the realization's shared policies are not stack-neutral, so the core's verification states the severity and disposition generically instead.

classification.note: One obligation naming no stack, runtime or path; carried verbatim so the core is neither weaker nor stronger.
Role-level preference with no concrete example; carried verbatim.
Refers only to the plan artifact in generic terms; carried verbatim.

Per-rule severity (3) and disposition (advisory), non-enforcement and the continued applicability of existing plan/source checks are generic enforcement facts -> core:verification; the shared:policy.pattern-guidance pointer is a realization id -> bunOnly.
Generic check instruction carried into the core's verification array exactly as the Bun rewrite states it: check that no planned hit path omits a required permission or mutation.
Stack-neutral applicability finding; the note is retained verbatim so the REQUIRED all-four-criteria, no-phase-restriction semantics are not weakened.
Stack-neutral task-term hint list; the note is retained verbatim so the terms stay an optional priority hint, not a trigger.

neutralityNotes: This rule is planning-level strategy guidance and was already stack-neutral; the core needs no structural facts from a profile, so profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty. The stack term 'wagon' in activation.fires[0] (the stack's bounded product slice, cf. layout.wagon_dir) was generalized to 'component'; the Bun wording remains in bun.json, which is delivered as the reference example. The activation fact notes (REQUIRED / OPTIONAL-hint semantics) are carried verbatim as note fields so the core is neither weaker nor stronger than the Bun rewrite. The shared:policy.pattern-guidance pointer is realization-specific and kept in bunOnly; per-rule severity and disposition live in core:verification, not in the profile. Per the round-2 feedback, core.verification[1] now carries the Bun instruction verbatim ('Check that no planned hit path omits a required permission or mutation.') with no exclusivity added, so it does not restrict what the check may verify.
